title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A fake cryptocurrency trading app created with AI technology deceived a Georgia investor by showing false account balances and fabricated transaction histories. The scammers used a fake overlay on a real app to manipulate what appeared on the investor's screen, making it appear that small initial investments and withdrawals were succeeding when no actual trades were occurring. The deception worked because the system presented false information as factual account data without any human verification of the underlying transactions.

The failure happened at the point where an investor trusted displayed information without independent confirmation of whether the trading platform was legitimate or whether their money actually existed in any account. A human check, such as attempting to verify the platform's registration or requesting official statements directly from the trading company, could have revealed the fraud before larger sums were committed. It is not established what specific AI techniques were used to generate the false interface or how the scammers obtained access to display their overlay on the victim's device.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. Jerry Dunaway was encouraged to invest through a mobile trading app, and the scammers built his trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts of money. However, the app was fake, created with artificial intelligence technology to show false account balances and trick investors into sending more money.

When Dunaway tried to withdraw a larger amount, he discovered the money was gone and called police. Gwinnett County investigators explained that while the trading app was real, scammers had created a fake overlay that manipulated what he saw on his screen. The couple is now warning others about the sophisticated tactics used by these criminals. Police say victims in these cases rarely recover their funds, but the Dunaways' children have started a GoFundMe to help their parents with expenses while they work with authorities.
